fields.subnational_unit: California; four water service providers in Southern California: City of Anaheim, City of Chino Hills, Cucamonga Valley Water District, City of Victorville / Victorville Water District
fields.population: residential customer accounts of four California water service providers in 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2023 (2020 excluded because of the COVID-19 shutoff moratorium)
fields.sample_size: 1,032,388 account-year observations in the chi-square tests across the four providers (accounts subject to disconnection or on a payment plan before and after SB 998)
fields.effect_measure: chi-square tests of association between SB 998 (pre versus post) and (RQ1) the number of water shutoffs for nonpayment and (RQ2) the number of payment plans; descriptive per-provider trends; comparative analysis of each provider's shutoff policy
fields.effect_estimate: RQ1: shutoffs for nonpayment fell significantly after SB 998 (chi-square(1, N = 1,032,388) = 20,098.971, p = 0.001). RQ2: payment plans rose significantly after SB 998 (chi-square(1, N = 1,032,388) = 6,694.463, p = 0.001). The author reads the rise in payment plans as customers being unable to keep their balances current; the 2022/23 water sales of all four providers declined. No effect size or confidence interval reported. A comparative table of each provider's shutoff policy (delinquency timeline, exceptions, assistance options, appeals, reconnection fees, tenant protections, timing limits) is given for Anaheim and Chino Hills (Tables 7-8) and the other providers.
fields.model_type: chi-square tests on pooled administrative counts, with descriptive per-provider time series and comparative policy analysis
fields.study_design: quantitative descriptive pre/post (before-after) study of a state statute using Public Records Act requests and utility financial reports; no comparison group
fields.risk_of_bias_rating: Some concern (appraised 2026-10-04 on the full text; supersedes the sparse-extraction 'High concern' of 2026-09-28; JBI Cross Sectional items 1-8: Yes,Yes,Yes,Yes,No,No,Unclear,No; 4/8 Yes). Basis: sample defined by provider and year (Yes); setting described (Yes); exposure = SB 998 timing (Yes); counts of shutoffs and payment plans from provider records (Yes); confounding not identified beyond excluding 2020 for the COVID moratorium (No), no strategy for confounding (No); outcome data came from Public Records Act requests of four providers chosen by data availability, reliability unreported (Unclear); chi-square on pooled counts with no effect size, no control for provider or trend (No). Caveat: an uncontrolled pre/post design cannot separate SB 998 from the pandemic, rate increases or the arrearage relief programme.
fields.section: Full text (dissertation): Abstract, Introduction, Research Questions, Research Design, Population/Sample, Results (RQ1-RQ2), Tables 2-8
fields.exact_location: Abstract p iv; RQs p12; design p48-50; chi-square results p58-60 (Tables 1-2); provider figures p60-64; policy analysis Tables 7-10 p67-70
fields.table: Tables 1-10 (chi-square tests; arrearage funds; financial statements; provider shutoff policy comparisons)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a quantitative descriptive pre/post analysis (DPA dissertation) of California SB 998 (the Water Shutoff Protection Act) across four Southern California providers, read in full text 2026-10-04. Shutoffs for nonpayment fell and payment plans rose significantly after SB 998 (chi-square on 1,032,388 account-years, p = 0.001); uncontrolled before-after design, no effect sizes, four providers chosen by data availability.
